surface_mechanism_description: The surface hydroxyl groups on the silica-coated AAO membranes react with the hydrophobic silane, PFDS, to form a covalently bonded self-assembled monolayer. This functionalization imparts chemical selectivity to the membrane, allowing for the selective transport of hydrophobic molecules over hydrophilic ones.
evidence: The silane reacts with the OH groups on the Al and Si surfaces to form a covalently bonded self-assembled monolayer. The hydrophobic PFDS-modiﬁed membranes showed enhanced sensitivity (ﬂux ratio 5.52) to the transport of hydrophobic molecules (tris(2,2 0 -bipyridyl)dichlororuthenium(II) hexahydrate (Rubpy), over hydrophilic molecules (rose bengal (RB)).
